metadata.title: Denzel Boston - Logs one catch in Week 6 win
metadata.description: Boston caught one of five targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 13-10 win over the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: It was easily the rookie wideout's least productive game of the season, but the Browns struggled as a whole to get anything going against Baltimore's pass defense. Deshaun Watson amassed just 164 passing yards. Boston was still second on the team in targets, seeing just one fewer than KC Concepcion. Boston will try to rebound in a softer matchup with the Titans next Sunday.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston logs one catch in Week 6
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston logged a season low in receptions (one) with 15 yards in a Week 6 win over Baltimore.
metadata.analysis: Boston has been a high point for Cleveland's offense, recording 40+ yards in the first five games to open his career. The rookie was still involved, earning five targets, though the opportunities did not translate into production. He should have another opportunity for a spike week against Tennessee in Week 7.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston a Bust for the First Time in Rookie Season
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston caught just one of his five targets for 15 receiving yards during Sunday's Week 6 win over the Baltimore Ravens. While Cleveland pulled off the upset victory at home, Boston was disappointing as he turned in the worst fantasy performance of his young career. This was the 22-year-old's first game with fewer than 8.0 PPR points, as well as just his second game with fewer than 12.5 PPR points. Prior to this week, Boston's name was gaining traction in Offensive Rookie of the Year conversations. Sunday's "bust" performance won't eliminate him from consideration for the award, but it definitely represents a stain on his season stat line. He'll look to bounce back in a much more favorable matchup against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston (foot) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Denzel Boston (foot) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens.
metadata.analysis: The rookie will be good to go on Sunday, despite dealing with a foot injury at practice throughout the week. He has been good through the first five weeks of the season and can safely be started in most league formats at this point.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston - Cleared to play against Ravens
metadata.description: Boston (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
metadata.analysis: A limited practice participant throughout the week, Boston should be fine for his usual workload unless there's an in-game setback Sunday. He's rarely left the field for Cleveland this season, and his big plays have been about the only bright spot on offense.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston (foot) limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie was limited for a second-straight practice on Thursday due to a nagging foot injury that he's dealing with. It looks like he will be available to play through it in Week 6, however, and fantasy managers should feel comfortable starting him if he doesn't carry an injury designation heading into the weekend.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston - Limited again Thursday
metadata.description: Boston (foot) remained limited at Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Boston has logged back-to-back limited practices to kick off Week 6 prep. The rookie wideout could still avoid taking an injury designation into Sunday's pivotal home game against the Ravens, especially if he can upgrade to full participation Thursday. Fellow rookie WR KC Concepcion (concussion) was also limited both Wednesday and Thursday. More opportunities could be available for Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond should one or both of Boston and Concepcion sit Sunday.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston Fitting in Nicely in Cleveland
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns rookie second-round wide receiver Denzel Boston is the team's leading receiver through the first five games of his first season in the NFL, catching 16 of his 29 targets for 330 yards and three touchdowns. Meanwhile, rookie first-round receiver KC Concepcion Jr. has 18 catches for 149 yards and no touchdowns, and he went down early in the Week 5 loss to the New York Jets with a scary concussion. Boston, 22, is on the Week 6 injury report with a foot injury, but he was limited in practice on Wednesday and should have a good chance to play this Sunday against the division-rival Baltimore Ravens. He has had at least seven targets in three of the last four games and would see an even bigger target share this weekend if Concepcion cannot clear the league's concussion protocol by the weekend. Boston is the current betting favorite for Offensive Rookie of the Year. The quick rise of both Boston and Concepcion has put Jerry Jeudy on the trade block. Boston should be considered a must-start against the Ravens, especially if Concepcion does not play.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston (foot) limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Denzel Boston was limited in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Boston should still be good to go for Sunday's game against the Ravens. His status is still worth monitoring in practice.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston - Limited by foot issue
metadata.description: Boston was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
metadata.analysis: The rookie second-round pick is making his first career appearance on the injury report, but his ability to practice on at least a limited basis to begin Week 6 prep is a good sign for his chances of playing Sunday against the Ravens. The current betting favorite for the Offensive Rookie of the Year Award, Boston has opened his career with a 16-330-3 receiving line on 29 targets through five games.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston - Scores third TD in Week 5 loss
metadata.description: Boston caught three of seven targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets.
metadata.analysis: Boston's 29-yard touchdown catch with 6:15 left in the fourth quarter gave the Browns a 12-10 lead, but Cleveland failed to hold that advantage. The rookie second-round pick has caught 16 of 29 targets for 330 yards and three touchdowns while exceeding 40 receiving yards in each of his first five NFL outings. KC Concepcion, who was drafted 15 picks ahead of Boston at 24th overall, exited Sunday's loss due to a concussion. Boston could get a larger share of targets from Deshaun Watson if Concepcion doesn't rejoin Cleveland's WR room in Week 6 against the Ravens.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston finds the end zone in Week 5 loss
metadata.description: Denzel Boston caught three of his seven targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in a 17-12 loss to the Jets in Week 5.
metadata.analysis: Boston's impressive rookie season continues. The emerging star pass-catcher hauled in a 29-yard touchdown from Deshaun Watson in the fourth quarter, giving the Browns a temporary lead. Boston has now caught three touchdowns through five games. He will be on the WR3 radar in Week 6's home game against the Ravens.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston Remains a Quality Play in Week 5
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston is RotoBaller's 29th-ranked wide receiver as he and the Browns go up against the New York Jets in Week 5. Boston has been incredibly productive to start his rookie season, averaging 71 yards per game and 21.8 yards per reception which recording a couple of touchdowns through his first four games. This past week during a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, Boston finished with four receptions for 89 yards. He is projected to score nine fantasy points against the Jets, who gave up a six-reception, 94-yard day to Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze last week.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston leads Browns with 89 receiving yards
metadata.description: Denzel Boston hauled in 4-of-7 targets for 89 yards in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Boston rebounded from just a so-so output in Week 3, leading the Browns in receiving yards Thursday night for the third time in four games. The rookie has quickly acclimated to the NFL, totaling 13 catches for an average of 71 yards per game and two touchdowns to this point.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston Continues to Make Big Plays Against Steelers
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston caught four of seven targets for 89 yards in the 27-24 win over division rival Pittsburgh. With quarterback Deshaun Watson off to a strong start to his 2026 season, Boston has produced, including a 60-yard reception down the left sideline. The rookie has now had three 45+ yard receptions in four games and remains a major part of the Browns' passing attack. He also saw elite usage again Thursday night, playing 95% of the snaps and running 100% of the routes. As long as Watson continues to play well and feed the Browns' young, talented weapons, Boston will be a WR3 in fantasy formats. However, reliance on big plays could make him a volatile option moving forward.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston - Continues thriving in Week 4 win
metadata.description: Boston brought in four of seven targets for 89 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The impressive start to Boston's NFL career continued Thursday, with the rookie second-round pick leading the Browns in receiving yards and tying for runner-up status with Quinshon Judkins in targets. The bulk of Boston's production came on an impressive 60-yard reception to kick off an early second-quarter possession that culminated in a Judkins two-yard touchdown run. Boston has quickly amassed a 13-284-2 line on 22 targets through his first four career games, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston Trying to Find End Zone Again in Week 4 Vs. Steelers
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston found the end zone in each of his first two NFL games. Connecting with Deshaun Watson against Jacksonville and Tampa Bay, Boston did not score a touchdown in Week 3's win over Carolina. He will look to get back in the end zone in Week 4's home game against Pittsburgh. Boston is averaging 21.7 yards per catch and has emerged as the Browns' big-play threat in the passing game. He is beginning to develop a rapport with Watson and looks like Cleveland's biggest threat on the outside. The Steelers will be without Joey Porter Jr. again on Thursday night, and Jalen Ramsey is questionable with a broken wrist that he hopes to play through. Look for Boston and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. to emerge as the top two targets in the passing game for Watson. Expect Boston to get back in the end zone against a depleted Steelers' secondary. Boston's big-play ability will be on display at home, and he won't rest until he finds his way into the end zone again.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston - Records two catches in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Boston caught two passes on four passes for 41 yards during the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday. He also caught a two-point conversion.
metadata.analysis: The rookie second-rounder was held without a catch until the fourth quarter, when he caught 28- and 13-yard passes from Deshaun Watson before the duo connected on a two-point conversion late in the fourth quarter to extend the Browns' lead to three points. Boston was unable to record a touchdown catch for a third-straight game, though he still finished Sunday's contest as the Browns' second-leading receiver behind tight end Harold Fannin (51). Boston, Fannin and rookie first-rounder KC Concepcion will continue to serve as Watson's top targets in the passing game, with Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond working in rotation. Boston will take a 9-195-2 receiving line (on 15 targets) into Thursday's AFC North showdown against the Steelers, whose secondary could be without starters Grant Delpit (shoulder) and Tyson Campbell (hip/knee/ankle).

metadata.title: Denzel Boston racks up 41 yards Sunday
metadata.description: Denzel Boston caught 2-of-4 targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers.
metadata.analysis: The rookie had an underwhelming performance against the Panthers, as he was only able to finish with two catches for 41 yards over the course of the afternoon. He has flashed potential but will likely continue to struggle with consistency over the course of the season.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston Offers Upside With Some Week 3 Risk
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston has earned a bigger role quickly, but Week 3 against Carolina comes with a little more uncertainty. The rookie has seven catches for 154 yards and two touchdowns through two games, while his targets climbed from four in the opener to seven last week. That growth is encouraging. At the same time, 101 of Boston's 154 receiving yards have come on touchdown catches of 46 and 55 yards, so his early fantasy production has leaned heavily on explosive plays. Carolina's outside coverage with Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson also gives him a tougher test than he saw in Tampa Bay. Boston remains a starter for Cleveland and is healthy heading into Sunday, so the opportunity should still be there. He sits at WR45 in RotoBaller's Week 3 rankings. Boston makes sense as a flex for managers chasing upside, while teams with a steadier alternative can reasonably take the safer route.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston a Good Start in Week 3 Vs. Panthers
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston is emerging as the leading target for Deshaun Watson and the Browns and has a touchdown in each of his first two games. Expect him to continue that success against a solid Panthers secondary in Week 3. The Browns return home for the home opener this week and expect Boston to show off his developing chemistry with Watson in what is a pretty tough matchup with the Panthers cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. In two games so far, Boston has totaled seven receptions for 154 receiving yards and two touchdowns. He's seen 11 targets total in both games combined, which is tied with KC Concepcion for the team lead in targets. Boston is making the most of his looks as he is averaging a team-best 22 yards per reception. Look for Boston to make a few big plays against the Panthers in Week 3 and continue his trend of making a splash in the passing game. The rookie second-round pick is riding the wave of a hot streak and fantasy managers should notice the trend and use Boston as a starting fantasy wide receiver.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston Looks Like a Must-Add After Week 2
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston has moved beyond speculative-stash territory after another productive game. The rookie caught five of seven targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-19 win over Tampa Bay, giving him 154 yards and two scores through his first two NFL games. Boston also led Cleveland in routes, targets and receiving yards in Week 2, which makes the performance more interesting than simply chasing his 55-yard touchdown. He drew only four targets in the opener, so the jump to seven is another encouraging sign. There is still some uncertainty with a rookie playing in an offense that may not support big receiving numbers every week, but Boston has already started both games and his role grew in Week 2. RotoBaller currently lists him as its top wide receiver waiver pickup and calls him a must-add. Fantasy managers in leagues where Boston remains available should treat him as a priority claim rather than a long-term stash.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston snags another touchdown Sunday
metadata.description: Denzel Boston caught 5-of-7 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: Boston connected with Deshaun Watson on a touchdown for the second straight week. He is seemingly emerging as the clear WR1 on the Browns offense. He'll hold some upside WR3 appeal next week for fantasy managers against the Panthers.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston - Scores another long TD in upset win
metadata.description: Boston caught five of seven targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 23-19 win over Tampa Bay on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Boston's big play was a 55-yard touchdown late in the third quarter to pull the Browns even with the Bucs at 16-16. The rookie wideout caught a deep crosser and spun off several would-be tackles and dashed to the end zone. It was Boston's second long touchdown in as many weeks to begin his pro career. Through two games, the second-round pick has seven catches for 154 yards and two scores on 11 targets. He's shaping up as a boom-or-bust fantasy WR4 headed into next Sunday's home date with the Panthers.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston Could Find Going Tough In Week 2 Matchup With Bucs
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston is coming off a Week 1 performance in which he snagged a touchdown pass from Deshaun Watson against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Boston caught two passes for 59 yards and a touchdown on his four targets. Boston looks like the main receiving target for Watson but is not worth starting in Week 2 at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Buccaneers held the explosive passing attack of the Cincinnati Bengals in check in their Week 1 matchup. The lead cornerbacks for the Bucs are Zyon McCollum and Benjamin Morrison and both did a good job of containing Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins of the Bengals. Boston should find the going tough against the Bucs in a passing attack that is much less formidable than the Bengals. Boston is a talented receiver and could do the most damage of the Browns receivers in this game, but there is not much that is trustworthy within the Browns' passing attack at the moment.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston a Solid Waiver-Wire Target After Encouraging NFL Debut
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston was one of his team's few bright spots in a 34-10 Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The 22-year-old recorded two catches for 59 yards and a touchdown on four targets. As long as quarterback Deshaun Watson remains the starter in Cleveland, it will be difficult for fantasy managers to have a great deal of trust in the Browns' passing game. Still, Boston led his team in receiving yards and finished tied for second in targets in his first NFL game. He also showed off his explosive ability with a 46-yard touchdown catch against the Jaguars, proving that he may still be able to provide fantasy production in an inefficient Cleveland offense. For his season-long upside, Boston profiles as a logical waiver wire target in fantasy leagues with 12 or more teams.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston snags bomb touchdown in loss
metadata.description: Denzel Boston caught two of four targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Boston had the Browns' only touchdown, though sadly it was in garbage time. His four targets tied with Jerry Jeudy for second on the team, an encouraging sign for his future usage as he gets further acclimated to the NFL game.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston - Hauls in 46-yard TD in debut
metadata.description: Boston caught two passes on four targets for 59 yards and a touchdown during the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: It wasn't until the third play of the fourth quarter that Boston made his first NFL catch, a 13-yard pass from Deshaun Watson, before the duo connected on a 46-yard touchdown pass on the first play following the two-minute warning. Boston finished Sunday's game as the Browns' leader in receiving yards while fellow rookie KC Concepcion led the team in catches (four) and targets (five). There figures to be some growing pains for the Browns' offense this season given the amount of young talent. Cleveland will stay on the road for a Week 2 matchup against Tampa Bay on Sept. 20.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston a Risky Flex in NFL Debut
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston will make his NFL debut Sunday against Jacksonville with a starting spot already in hand. The rookie is listed alongside Jerry Jeudy and KC Concepcion Jr., and Cleveland liked him enough to take him 39th overall after a 62-catch, 881-yard, 11-touchdown final season at Washington. Boston also made plenty of contested catches during camp. The preseason did not give us much to work with, though. He caught one pass for 15 yards across three games. Jacksonville allowed 25 passing touchdowns last season, but the Jaguars also picked off 22 passes, and Deshaun Watson is not exactly lifting the outlook for Cleveland's receivers right now. RotoBaller has Boston at WR70 for Week 1, while its current start-sit guidance recommends keeping the Browns' wideouts to deeper leagues with multiple flex spots. Boston is worth rostering because the role could grow quickly. For Sunday, fantasy managers should keep him on the bench unless they are digging deep for a flex.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston a Must-Add Wide Receiver Amidst Preseason Buzz
metadata.description: After recording over 1,700 receiving yards and 20 touchdowns across his final two collegiate seasons at the University of Washington, wide receiver Denzel Boston was selected 39th overall in the 2026 NFL Draft by the Cleveland Browns. Boston has reportedly been an impressive performer throughout the preseason in Browns camp, and he could be in line for a significant role in the Cleveland offense right away. With fellow rookie KC Concepcion and veteran wideout Jerry Jeudy as his primary competition, Boston has a legitimate chance to emerge as the Browns' WR1 before the end of the year. Despite the underwhelming quarterback situation in Cleveland, Boston profiles as a must-add wide receiver in any fantasy league where he remains unrostered ahead of 2026.

metadata.title: Denzel Boston is Gaining Traction After Strong Showing in Camp
metadata.description: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston has been one of the most impressive players in this offense during training camp. The Browns are extremely pleased with the results they've been getting from the second-round rookie. According to the Browns' unofficial depth chart, Boston is listed as a starting wideout alongside Jerry Jeudy. The Browns don't have many viable options to count on as pass-catchers, so both Boston and fellow rookie KC Concepcion could play significant roles right away. The 22-year-old is looking like a sleeper target in the late rounds during redraft formats. It might take some time, but fantasy managers shouldn't be surprised if Boston makes a big impact in Cleveland this upcoming season.
